// FatalError is for CLI front-ends: it detects gravitational/trace debugging
// information, sends it to the logger, strips it off and prints a clean message to stderr
func FatalError(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, UserMessageFromError(err))
	os.Exit(1)
}

// GetIterations provides a simple way to add iterations to the test
// by setting environment variable "ITERATIONS", by default it returns 1
func GetIterations() int {
	out := os.Getenv(teleport.IterationsEnvVar)
	if out == "" {
		return 1
	}
	iter, err := strconv.Atoi(out)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	log.Debugf("Starting tests with %v iterations.", iter)
	return iter
}

item.text:
Updated `ContextReader` to restore the terminal when a password read is canceled or the reader closes, then return to a clean state so later reads can proceed. Added `NotifyExit` for the global stdin reader and called it when `tsh` exits.

The prompt package tests and race test pass. I stopped the broader `tsh` build check after prolonged dependency compilation, so that check remains unverified.
